newsitem.title: CHILE: NAFTA would have prevented trade spats - Chile.
newsitem.headline: NAFTA would have prevented trade spats - Chile.

text.p: Looming trade disputes between Chilean and U.S. salmon raisers and forestry firms could have been avoided had Chile been a member of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), said Chilean President Eduardo Frei.
"If we had the NAFTA agreement with the United States, this would not be happening," Frei told reporters Wednesday.
"This is why we have been seeking (an agreement), and this shows clearly the use of international accords."

Chile was invited to join NAFTA, which groups the United States, Mexico and Canada, in December 1994, but talks have gone nowhere because of political difficulties in Washington which have delayed discussion of "fast-track" legislation.
Chile already has a free trade agreement with Mexico and an agreement with Canada should come fully into force Thursday provided it is approved by the Chilean Senate in a vote Wednesday.

Chilean salmon producers have been accused by their U.S. counterparts of dumping and of receiving illegal subsidies. The government has said it will defend the salmon raisers against the subsidy charges which have been filed at the U.S. Commerce Department.

A second dispute emerged last week when Chilean forestry companies denounced a federal court ruling prohibiting the U.S. government from issuing new import permits for logs and wood chips from three countries including Chile.
"Developing countries always suffer higher taxes and barriers when they export higher value products," said Frei.
"International agreements protect our producers, institutionalize and create arbitration systems to avoid this type of problem."
The trade spats served to reinforce Chile's policy of building networks of trade treaties to phase down barriers with its commercial partners, he said.
"When we don't have signed agreements, we suffer this type of situation...So as a result, we will insist on reaching international accords," he said.
Frei confirmed that Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia will travel shortly to Washington for talks on the disputes with U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley.
"We will take all steps (necessary) as a government as we have to take great care with quasi-tariff barriers, and we will give our full support to the companies," he said.

Chilean businessmen have blamed the spats on protectionism from U.S. companies and have been careful to avoid pinning responsibility on the Clinton administration. ((-- Rodrigo Martinez, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
